01
Chapter
The Problem

Ethereum stores everything — every balance, every contract, every slot of storage — in one structure called the global state. Accessing or proving any of it today costs an enormous amount of data.

To run a node you must download and hold the full state (~200 GB). That is the barrier: committing hundreds of gigabytes just to check whether a transaction is valid.

200GB
Full State Today
3.8KB
Per-Account Proof
↑
Proof Size Growing

The bottleneck is the data structure itself: the Merkle Patricia Tree. Proving one account means revealing sibling hashes at every level — and they add up fast.

The goal: a node that can verify a block using only a small witness bundled with it — never storing the full 200 GB. That is a stateless client, and Verkle Trees make it possible.
02
Chapter
Merkle Patricia Trees

Ethereum's current tree keeps data at the leaves; each internal node is just the hash of its children. To prove any leaf, you need a full path of sibling hashes up to the root.

Analogy: proving you're on a flight's passenger list by showing half the list at every level of a hierarchy. More passengers, bigger proof.
Merkle Tree — Click a Leaf
Click any leaf (bottom row) to see the proof path highlighted in red
// each node is a hash of its children
parent = Hash(child₁ || child₂ || … || childₙ)
// proving one child requires ALL siblings

For Ethereum's hexary tree (branching 16, depth ~8), each proof needs up to 120 hashes ≈ 3.8 KB per account. Prove 500 accounts in a block and you're shipping ~1.9 MB of witness — impractical for stateless nodes.

03
Chapter
Verkle Trees

Verkle = Vector Commitment + Merkle. Same shape, but internal nodes no longer store hashes — they store polynomial commitments.

A polynomial commitment binds a whole set of children to one compact point. Later you can prove any single child without revealing the rest. No siblings needed.

Verkle Tree — Click a Leaf
Click any leaf — the proof only needs ONE commitment per level
3.8KB
Merkle Proof
150B
Verkle Proof
25×
Smaller
04
Chapter
How It Works

The engine is a polynomial commitment (IPA). Four steps:

Step 1
Encode children as a polynomial
A node with 256 children c₀…c₂₅₅ builds p(x) where p(i)=cᵢ. Every child is a point on the curve.
Step 2
Commit to the polynomial
Elliptic-curve math compresses p(x) into one commitment point C — 32–48 bytes fingerprinting all 256 children.
Step 3
Prove any single child
A short proof π shows p(i)=cᵢ without revealing other children. Anyone with C verifies instantly.
Bonus
Aggregate all proofs into one
Every leaf touched in a block merges into a single constant-size proof. 500 accounts, one proof.
Polynomial Commitment — Click Points
The curve encodes all children. Click any dot to "prove" that value.
// Merkle — need siblings
proof = depth × (branching−1) × 32 bytes

// Verkle — just path commitments
proof = depth × 32 bytes // no siblings!

06
Chapter
Stateless Clients

The payoff: with Verkle Trees a node stores no state at all. It verifies each block from the tiny witness bundled with it.

200GB
Full Node Today
~200KB
Stateless Node
1M×
Size Reduction

The block proposer attaches a witness — a compact Verkle proof covering every slot the block touched. Any receiver verifies the block from witness + header alone. No state storage needed.

Why it matters: today a validator needs costly hardware and 200 GB of disk. Stateless clients could run a validator on a phone — more validators, more decentralisation.
ZK synergy: Verkle proofs are polynomial-based — the same math as ZK-SNARKs — so Ethereum's future ZK layer can verify Verkle witnesses directly.
07
Chapter
Ethereum Roadmap

Verkle Trees are part of "The Verge" — one of five phases on Ethereum's post-Merge roadmap.

Done
The Merge
Proof of Stake. Energy use dropped 99.95%.
Done
The Surge
EIP-4844 (Dencun) blobs — 10× cheaper rollup data.
Active ◀
The Verge — Verkle Trees (EIP-6800, EIP-7748)
Replacing Merkle Patricia Trees. On devnets now — exactly what this site explores. Unlocks stateless clients.
Soon
The Purge
Remove historical-data requirements. With stateless clients, nodes need almost no storage.
Future
The Splurge
ZK-EVM verification, account abstraction, fully ZK-proven execution.
Takeaway: Verkle Trees are the biggest cryptographic change to Ethereum since the Merge — the prerequisite for every upgrade that follows.

The baseline Verkle improves on, running for real. This builds a Merkle tree with genuine SHA-256 (Web Crypto) — the exact structure Ethereum uses today. Build account state, watch the root recompute, generate an inclusion proof, verify it, then tamper with the claim and watch verification fail. Verkle swaps these hash nodes for polynomial commitments to shrink the proof — but the proof-and-tamper logic you see here is identical and 100% real. State persists in your browser.
